params.wrong_if: Priya's termly time cost, the £4,200 annual write-off figure, or the two named pupil dropouts turn out not to recur year on year as stated.

text: Filed as a business-level decision: the answer names a person (Priya), a frequency (two days every term, recurring annually), and a cost (£4,200 written-off instruments plus two named Year 9 pupils who dropped out) — that's the who/how-often/at-what-cost the question asks for.

params.wrong_if: The paper book and spreadsheet turn out to capture swaps accurately between office visits, or the business manager sees write-offs before July.

text: Filed at business level: the answer names the current process (paper loan book, September spreadsheet rebuild) and three specific, checkable shortcomings — unrecorded swaps, drift by half-term, and the business manager's July blind spot on write-offs.

params.wrong_if: Peripatetic teachers turn out to record handovers, consent slips return promptly, or Priya's end-of-year reconciliation is not the actual mechanism catching drift.

text: Filed at stakeholder level under seq 5: the answer goes beyond the documented sign-and-consent flow to name the actual undocumented steps — corridor handovers, case-swapping, late slips, and Priya's clipboard reconciliation — with enough specificity to be checked against.

params.wrong_if: Peripatetic teachers adopt handover recording regardless of speed, or Tom's monthly write-off visibility turns out not to change behaviour, showing the named bet wasn't the real constraint.

text: Filed at solution level under seq 6: the answer names three falsifiable conditions and explicitly flags which one is the real bet — the thirty-second phone handover for hourly-paid peripatetic teachers — rather than listing things already known to be true.

params.wrong_if: The two-teacher, two-week test does not isolate the handover-recording assumption from the app-visibility or Priya's-trust assumptions, or its result fails to predict behaviour at full rollout.

text: Filed at transition level under seq 7: the answer isolates a single riskiest assumption — hourly-paid peripatetic teachers with no incentive to adopt anything — and names a bounded test (two teachers, two weeks, alone) rather than a broad validation round that would confound it with the other two conditions.

params.wrong_if: Tom turns out to already see the loan book or delegate sign-off elsewhere, or the head of department is not the one accountable to governors for the July loss report.

text: Filed at stakeholder level under seq 2: the answer names three distinct roles — Priya (pain), Tom (budget, with a stated £1,500/year ceiling), and the head of department (reputational exposure to governors) — and states plainly they are not the same person, with a concrete fact (Tom has never seen the loan book) rather than a generic persona.

params.wrong_if: The two-week appetite slips once work starts, or the handover cannot be shipped without also building the parent view or redesigning the parent app.

text: Filed at transition level under seq 7: the appetite (two weeks, one developer) is fixed before scope, and the answer names what gets cut — parent view deferred, no app redesign — rather than producing an estimate, which is the form Shape Up asks for here.

params.wrong_if: The parent app turns out unable to embed a read-only page and no termly-email fallback is built, or the no-signature-with-seven-day-reversal rule gets revisited mid-build rather than settled now.

text: Filed at transition level under seq 7: each sub-question is answered directly — no new technical work, the unchecked embed assumption is settled now with a named fallback, and the hard decision (no-signature handover with a seven-day reversal window) is fixed in advance rather than left for the build.

params.wrong_if: A mid-build request for payments, booking, condition photos, county-system integration, or messaging is absorbed into scope rather than deferred to a later term.

text: Filed at transition level under seq 7: the answer names five specific exclusions and a rule for what happens when one is requested mid-build — a real no-gos list rather than an absent one that leaves scope to be cut later under pressure.

params.wrong_if: Losses continue to be attributed to Priya in practice despite the named-handover trail, or the head of department's written agreement to sign the termly report does not hold once losses actually occur.

text: Filed at stakeholder level under seq 5: the answer names who is accountable today (Priya, regardless of what she saw), states the deliberate shift the design makes (accountability follows the last recorded handover, the head of department signs the loss report instead), and grounds it in a written agreement rather than a flag nobody owns.

params.wrong_if: The tool's timestamp count and Priya's end-of-term count diverge enough to dispute the 70% figure, or the threshold is reached but for reasons unrelated to teacher adoption.

text: Filed at transition level under seq 7: the stop condition names a specific, observable threshold (under 70% same-day recording by end of spring term), a measurement method, and the fallback action — a result that can actually occur and be checked, not one that describes an impossibility.

params.wrong_if: A model is added to the product without being run against the three-year loan-outcomes set or without clearing 95% on it, or Priya is not the one who signs off the eval.

text: Filed at solution level under seq 13: the answer correctly names that no model exists so no eval currently applies, and pre-commits the full form the question asks for should one ever be proposed — named set (three years of loan records with known outcomes), named owner (Priya), and a stated pass rate (95%) — rather than dodging the question or citing a generic benchmark.
